New machine. Its objects are: riliper, migapus, famagin, vubidan, belonek, ninives.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half the objects. This splits the 30 possible answers (15 pairs × 2 rules) evenly, 15 for "lit" and 15 for "not lit".

TEST: riliper, migapus, famagin
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

After the first test, 15 possibilities remain. If needs = one, both nexioms are among vubidan, belonek and ninives (3 pairs). If needs = two, any pair is possible except one entirely inside riliper/migapus/famagin (12 pairs). With 4 tests I can tell apart at most 16 cases, so each test must split the remaining possibilities about evenly.

This test splits them 8 lit and 7 not lit:
- **Lit (8):** all 3 needs-one pairs, plus 5 needs-two pairs: vubidan+belonek, vubidan+riliper, vubidan+migapus, belonek+riliper, belonek+migapus.
- **Not lit (7):** only needs-two pairs: vubidan+ninives, belonek+ninives, ninives+riliper, ninives+migapus, ninives+famagin, vubidan+famagin, belonek+famagin.

TEST: vubidan, belonek, riliper, migapus
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Eight possibilities remain:
- **Needs one:** vubidan+belonek, vubidan+ninives, belonek+ninives
- **Needs two:** vubidan+belonek, vubidan+riliper, vubidan+migapus, belonek+riliper, belonek+migapus

This test splits them 4 and 4:
- **Lit (4):** needs-one vubidan+belonek, needs-one vubidan+ninives, needs-two vubidan+riliper, needs-two vubidan+migapus.
- **Not lit (4):** needs-one belonek+ninives, needs-two vubidan+belonek, needs-two belonek+riliper, needs-two belonek+migapus.

Two more tests can then separate whichever 4 remain.

TEST: vubidan, riliper, migapus
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Four possibilities remain:
- needs one: belonek+ninives
- needs two: vubidan+belonek
- needs two: belonek+riliper
- needs two: belonek+migapus

This test splits them 2 and 2:
- **Lit (2):** needs-one belonek+ninives (belonek alone is enough), needs-two belonek+riliper.
- **Not lit (2):** needs-two vubidan+belonek, needs-two belonek+migapus.

My last test can then tell apart whichever 2 are left.

TEST: belonek, riliper
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Two possibilities remain, both needing two nexioms:
- vubidan+belonek
- belonek+migapus

This test tells them apart. If it lights up, the nexioms are vubidan and belonek. If it doesn't, they are belonek and migapus.

TEST: vubidan, belonek
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The last test did not light up, so the nexioms are belonek and migapus, and this machine needs both of them together.

This fits all five results:
- **Test 1** (riliper, migapus, famagin) had only migapus, so it did not light up.
- **Test 2** (vubidan, belonek, riliper, migapus) had both nexioms, so it lit up.
- **Test 3** (vubidan, riliper, migapus) had only migapus, so it did not light up.
- **Test 4** (belonek, riliper) had only belonek, so it did not light up.
- **Test 5** (vubidan, belonek) had only belonek, so it did not light up.

ANSWER: nexioms = belonek, migapus; needs = two

New machine. Its objects are: lidenol, vufanir, kusazu, natuma, girufik, gilavos.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing three of the six objects. This splits the 30 possible cases evenly: 15 would light the machine and 15 would not.

TEST: lidenol, vufanir, kusazu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first test lit up, so 15 of the 30 cases remain:
- **Needs one (12 cases):** at least one nexiom is among lidenol, vufanir and kusazu.
- **Needs two (3 cases):** both nexioms are among lidenol, vufanir and kusazu.

Testing lidenol with natuma splits these well:
- **It lights up in 7 cases:** these all need one nexiom, with the pair containing lidenol or natuma.
- **It stays dark in 8 cases:** these are the remaining needs-one pairs plus all 3 needs-two cases.

TEST: lidenol, natuma
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Test 2 stayed dark, so lidenol and natuma are not nexioms in a needs-one machine. That leaves 8 cases:
- **Needs one (5 cases):** vufanir+kusazu, vufanir+girufik, vufanir+gilavos, kusazu+girufik, kusazu+gilavos.
- **Needs two (3 cases):** lidenol+vufanir, lidenol+kusazu, vufanir+kusazu.

Three tests can tell 8 cases apart only if each test splits the remaining cases exactly in half. Testing vufanir with girufik does that:
- **It lights up in 4 cases:** all needs-one, namely vufanir+kusazu, vufanir+girufik, vufanir+gilavos and kusazu+girufik.
- **It stays dark in 4 cases:** needs-one kusazu+gilavos, plus all 3 needs-two cases.

TEST: vufanir, girufik
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Test 3 stayed dark, which leaves 4 cases:
- **Needs one (1 case):** kusazu+gilavos.
- **Needs two (3 cases):** lidenol+vufanir, lidenol+kusazu, vufanir+kusazu.

Testing lidenol with kusazu splits these 2 and 2:
- **It lights up in 2 cases:** needs-one kusazu+gilavos, or needs-two lidenol+kusazu.
- **It stays dark in 2 cases:** needs-two lidenol+vufanir, or needs-two vufanir+kusazu.

The last test can then tell the final two cases apart.

TEST: lidenol, kusazu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Test 4 lit up, so two cases remain:
- **Needs one:** kusazu+gilavos.
- **Needs two:** lidenol+kusazu.

Testing gilavos alone separates them. If it lights up, the machine needs one nexiom and gilavos is one of them. If it stays dark, gilavos is not a nexiom and it must be the needs-two case.

TEST: gilavos
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Gilavos alone stayed dark, so it is not a nexiom, which rules out the needs-one case of kusazu and gilavos. The only case left is that the machine needs two, with lidenol and kusazu as the nexioms.

This fits all five results:
- **Test 1 (lidenol, vufanir, kusazu):** both nexioms were on it, so it lit up.
- **Test 2 (lidenol, natuma):** only lidenol was on it, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 3 (vufanir, girufik):** neither nexiom was on it, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 4 (lidenol, kusazu):** both nexioms were on it, so it lit up.
- **Test 5 (gilavos):** neither nexiom was on it, so it stayed dark.

ANSWER: nexioms = lidenol, kusazu; needs = two

New machine. Its objects are: ludekor, tumeduk, gemoton, bibavu, kinidos, kirevin.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

There are 15 possible pairs and 2 possible rules, so 30 cases in all. Five yes/no tests give at most 32 outcomes, so each test needs to split the remaining cases roughly in half. Testing three objects does this. In "needs one" mode it lights for the 12 pairs that touch the set. In "needs two" mode it lights for the 3 pairs inside it. That gives 15 cases where it lights and 15 where it stays dark.

TEST: ludekor, tumeduk, gemoton
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

15 cases remain. Under "needs one", the nexiom pair includes at least one of ludekor, tumeduk or gemoton, which leaves 12 pairs. Under "needs two", both nexioms are among those three, which leaves 3 pairs.

Testing ludekor with bibavu splits these cases roughly in half:
- **Lights (7 cases):** all under "needs one". These are the 5 pairs containing ludekor, plus bibavu–tumeduk and bibavu–gemoton.
- **Stays dark (8 cases):** the other 5 "needs one" pairs, plus all 3 "needs two" pairs.

TEST: ludekor, bibavu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

8 cases remain:
- **Needs one (5):** the pair contains tumeduk or gemoton but neither ludekor nor bibavu. That leaves tumeduk–gemoton, tumeduk–kinidos, tumeduk–kirevin, gemoton–kinidos and gemoton–kirevin.
- **Needs two (3):** ludekor–tumeduk, ludekor–gemoton and tumeduk–gemoton.

Testing tumeduk with kinidos splits these 4/4:
- **Lights (4):** under "needs one", the pairs tumeduk–gemoton, tumeduk–kinidos, tumeduk–kirevin and gemoton–kinidos.
- **Stays dark (4):** gemoton–kirevin under "needs one", plus all three "needs two" pairs.

TEST: tumeduk, kinidos
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Four cases remain:
- **Needs one (1):** gemoton–kirevin.
- **Needs two (3):** ludekor–tumeduk, ludekor–gemoton and tumeduk–gemoton.

Testing ludekor with gemoton splits these 2/2:
- **Lights (2):** gemoton–kirevin under "needs one", or ludekor–gemoton under "needs two". Testing gemoton alone would then tell these apart.
- **Stays dark (2):** ludekor–tumeduk or tumeduk–gemoton, both under "needs two". Testing ludekor with tumeduk would then tell these apart.

TEST: ludekor, gemoton
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Only two cases remain, and both are "needs two": ludekor–tumeduk or tumeduk–gemoton. Testing ludekor with tumeduk decides it. If it lights, the pair is ludekor–tumeduk. If it stays dark, the pair is tumeduk–gemoton.

TEST: ludekor, tumeduk
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The last test stayed dark, so the pair is not ludekor–tumeduk. That leaves only tumeduk–gemoton under "needs two".

This fits every result:
- **Test 1 (ludekor, tumeduk, gemoton): lit.** Both nexioms were on the machine.
- **Tests 2–5: all dark.** None of them had both tumeduk and gemoton on the machine.

ANSWER: nexioms = tumeduk, gemoton; needs = two

New machine. Its objects are: vitado, maluzu, mapenu, kezokil, dekemar, fibemu.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

With 15 possible pairs and 2 rules, there are 30 possibilities, and 5 yes/no tests give at most 32 outcomes. So each test needs to split the remaining possibilities roughly in half.

Putting three objects on the machine does that:
- **Lights up (15 cases):** 12 one-nexiom cases where at least one nexiom is in the group, plus 3 two-nexiom cases where both are in it.
- **Stays dark (15 cases):** 3 one-nexiom cases where both nexioms are outside the group, plus 12 two-nexiom cases where not both are in it.

TEST: vitado, maluzu, mapenu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.
That move could not be read (no line starting with TEST: or ANSWER:). End your message with one TEST: or ANSWER: line in the form given.

The machine lit up when vitado, maluzu and mapenu were on it, so 15 possibilities remain:
- **Needs one (12 cases):** at least one nexiom is among vitado, maluzu and mapenu.
- **Needs two (3 cases):** both nexioms are among vitado, maluzu and mapenu.

Testing vitado and kezokil together splits these 7 to 8:
- **Lights up (7 cases):** all needs-one. The pair includes vitado (5 cases) or includes kezokil with maluzu or mapenu (2 cases).
- **Stays dark (8 cases):** 5 needs-one cases plus all 3 needs-two cases. No needs-two pair can contain both vitado and kezokil.

TEST: vitado, kezokil
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine stayed dark with vitado and kezokil, so 8 possibilities remain:
- **Needs one (5 cases):** neither vitado nor kezokil is a nexiom, and at least one of maluzu or mapenu is. The possible pairs are maluzu–mapenu, maluzu–dekemar, maluzu–fibemu, mapenu–dekemar and mapenu–fibemu.
- **Needs two (3 cases):** both nexioms are among vitado, maluzu and mapenu, but not both vitado and kezokil. The possible pairs are vitado–maluzu, vitado–mapenu and maluzu–mapenu.

Testing maluzu and dekemar together splits these 4 to 4:
- **Lights up (4 cases):** all needs-one. The pair is maluzu–mapenu, maluzu–dekemar, maluzu–fibemu or mapenu–dekemar.
- **Stays dark (4 cases):** needs-one mapenu–fibemu, plus all 3 needs-two cases. No needs-two pair is exactly maluzu and dekemar.

Either way, two more tests can each halve what is left.

TEST: maluzu, dekemar
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine stayed dark with maluzu and dekemar, so 4 possibilities remain:
- **Needs one (1 case):** mapenu–fibemu. This is the only needs-one pair with neither maluzu nor dekemar.
- **Needs two (3 cases):** vitado–maluzu, vitado–mapenu or maluzu–mapenu. None of these needs only maluzu and dekemar, so all three survive.

Testing vitado and mapenu together splits these 2 to 2:
- **Lights up (2 cases):** needs-one mapenu–fibemu, because mapenu is present, or needs-two vitado–mapenu. Testing mapenu alone would then settle it: it lights only if the machine needs one.
- **Stays dark (2 cases):** needs-two vitado–maluzu or maluzu–mapenu. Testing vitado and maluzu together would then settle it: it lights only if the pair is vitado–maluzu.

TEST: vitado, mapenu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The machine stayed dark with vitado and mapenu, so the machine must need two nexioms. Only 2 possibilities remain:
- **vitado–maluzu:** this pair is not ruled out by any test so far.
- **maluzu–mapenu:** this pair is not ruled out either.

Testing vitado and maluzu together settles it. If it lights up, the nexioms are vitado and maluzu. If it stays dark, they are maluzu and mapenu.

TEST: vitado, maluzu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The machine lit up with vitado and maluzu on it. So the nexioms are vitado and maluzu, and the machine needs both of them together.

This fits all five tests:
- **Test 1 (vitado, maluzu, mapenu):** both nexioms were on, so it lit up.
- **Test 2 (vitado, kezokil):** only vitado was on, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 3 (maluzu, dekemar):** only maluzu was on, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 4 (vitado, mapenu):** only vitado was on, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 5 (vitado, maluzu):** both nexioms were on, so it lit up.

A needs-one machine is ruled out, because test 2 would have lit up from vitado alone.

ANSWER: nexioms = vitado, maluzu; needs = two
